label: 5G
plain_descriptions: fifth generation cellular technology delivering high speeds and ultra-responsive connections
advanced telecommunications network standard uniting broadband smartphones and industrial machine connectivity
summary: The fifth-generation telecommunications standard for broadband cellular networks, defined by enhanced mobile broadband, massive machine connectivity, and ultra-reliable low-latency links.

label: A/B testing

controlled trial where real users are randomly split to measure which design drives higher conversions
summary: A randomized experimental method where two variants of a digital experience are shown to visitors simultaneously to determine which drives superior outcomes.

label: Accelerometer
plain_descriptions: sensor that detects motion, shakes, and the pull of gravity on a device
microchip that measures changes in speed and tells a phone to rotate its screen
summary: An electromechanical sensor that measures proper acceleration—the physical acceleration experienced by an object relative to freefall, including the gravitational vector.

label: Acceptance criteria
plain_descriptions: specific checklist of conditions that a user story must satisfy before being marked complete
unambiguous rules showing developers and testers exactly how a feature should behave
summary: A predefined set of conditions, behaviors, and boundary checks that a specific user story must satisfy to be accepted.

label: Accrual accounting

financial reporting principle linking revenues with related expenses regardless of payment dates
summary: The financial reporting method recording revenues when earned and expenses when incurred, regardless of the timing of cash receipts or disbursements.

label: ACID

the core database promise that financial transactions either succeed 100% or leave no trace
summary: A set of four fundamental properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) that guarantee database transactions are processed reliably.

label: Actuator

component that moves or controls a physical mechanism in response to a signal
summary: An output device that converts electrical control signals into physical movement, force, or mechanical displacement.

label: Impression
plain_descriptions: every single time an advertisement appears on someone's screen
the total view count of an ad including repeat sightings by the same person
summary: A metric recording each individual occurrence of an advertisement being fetched and rendered on a user's viewport screen.

label: Analog-to-digital converter (ADC)
plain_descriptions: electronic circuit that converts smooth continuous physical voltages into discrete digital numbers
sensor-reading chip that turns real-world voltage levels into numbers a computer can process
summary: An electronic circuit system that samples a continuous analog voltage waveform and quantizes it into discrete multi-bit digital numeric values.

label: Agent
plain_descriptions: an AI system that plans steps and uses tools to achieve goals independently
a software assistant that observes its environment, takes actions, and completes tasks
summary: An autonomous AI system that reasons over objectives, breaks goals into sequential steps, and interacts with tools and environments to complete tasks.

label: AI alignment
plain_descriptions: ensuring that artificial intelligence systems act in harmony with human values and intended goals
designing AI models that do what users genuinely want without causing harmful side effects
summary: The field of artificial intelligence research dedicated to ensuring that AI systems reliably pursue human goals, ethical principles, and safety boundaries without harmful unintended consequences.

label: Benchmark
plain_descriptions: standardized test suites used to measure AI model accuracy and hardware speed
common evaluation exams allowing different AI systems to be fairly compared
summary: A standardized test suite and measurement protocol used to evaluate and compare the accuracy, throughput, latency, or energy efficiency of models and hardware.

label: Alerting
plain_descriptions: mechanism that pages or notifies engineers when system metrics cross danger thresholds
automated notification system turning telemetry data into urgent action items for on-call teams
summary: The automated process of evaluating metrics and logs against rules to notify human operators when unexpected conditions occur.

label: Algorithm
plain_descriptions: unambiguous, step-by-step recipe of instructions designed to solve a specific problem
computational formula that processes input data and produces a deterministic output
summary: A well-defined, finite sequence of unambiguous instructions designed to perform a specific computational computation or solve a problem.

label: Anonymous source
plain_descriptions: an informant providing facts to a journalist without their identity being publicly disclosed
a protected whistleblower or insider quoted without their real name
summary: An informant who shares factual intelligence or testimony with a reporter under an agreement that their personal identity will remain confidential.

label: Ansible
plain_descriptions: agentless tool for configuring servers and automating software setups via SSH
automation engine using YAML playbooks to install and manage software across machines
summary: An open-source automation engine that automates cloud provisioning, configuration management, and application deployment without installing agents on managed nodes.

label: Apache Airflow
plain_descriptions: a tool that schedules and monitors multi-step data pipelines using Python code
an automated task manager that runs database extraction and report scripts in orderly sequence
summary: An open-source platform used to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor complex data engineering workflows.

label: Apache Flink
plain_descriptions: an open-source framework designed for real-time calculations on continuous data streams
a high-speed event computation engine that tracks accurate running totals without stopping
summary: An open-source distributed engine engineered for low-latency stateful stream calculations across finite and infinite event feeds.

label: Apache Kafka
plain_descriptions: a distributed software platform that records continuous streams of records across multiple servers
an enterprise real-time message bus that stores event history reliably and replays events on demand
summary: A distributed event streaming platform used for high-throughput data pipelines, streaming analytics, and system integration.

label: Apache Spark
plain_descriptions: a fast big-data computing engine that processes massive datasets in computer memory
an open-source framework for running large data transformations and machine learning across clusters
summary: An open-source distributed computing framework designed for fast processing of large-scale datasets using in-memory abstractions.

label: Application Programming Interface (API)
plain_descriptions: a defined bridge that allows two software systems to talk to each other
a digital waiter taking requests from one application to another
summary: A set of defined rules, protocols, and endpoints enabling different software applications to communicate and exchange data.

label: Endpoint
plain_descriptions: the specific web address where an app sends requests to get certain information
a digital front door where external software asks a server to do something
summary: A dedicated network address and URL path exposed by an API where clients access a specific service or resource.

label: API gateway
plain_descriptions: single front entrance that directs client requests to appropriate backend services
entry server handling auth, throttling, and routing for microservices
summary: An intermediary server pattern that acts as a single point of entry for external clients, routing requests to internal microservices while handling cross-cutting concerns.

label: API key
plain_descriptions: a unique secret string that an application sends to identify itself when calling a web service
a digital password used by programs to track usage and control access to an API
summary: A unique alphanumeric string passed by an application to authenticate the calling program and track its API consumption.

label: Application performance monitoring (APM)
plain_descriptions: software that watches web applications from the inside to detect slow database queries and code bottlenecks
end-to-end monitoring tool that measures user transaction speeds, error rates, and system dependencies
summary: The practice and tooling dedicated to observing the availability, software errors, and transaction performance of complex software applications.

label: Arduino
plain_descriptions: open-source microcontroller board and software platform for controlling physical electronics
easy-to-program electronic prototyping board that reads buttons and turns on motors
summary: An open-source electronics prototyping platform encompassing programmable microcontroller hardware boards and a simplified software development environment for controlling physical actuators and sensors.

label: Array
plain_descriptions: ordered collection of elements stored at contiguous memory locations accessed by zero-based indices
basic sequence list where each item is identified by its numerical position
summary: A linear data structure consisting of a collection of elements identified by index or key, stored in contiguous memory locations.

label: Aspect ratio
plain_descriptions: the proportional relationship between the width and height of an image or screen
screen dimension proportion such as 16:9 widescreen or 9:16 vertical smartphone format
summary: The proportional ratio describing the relationship of an image, frame, or display device's width relative to its height.

label: Asset
plain_descriptions: anything of economic value owned or controlled by a person or company
valuable resource expected to generate future financial benefits or cash
summary: A present economic resource controlled by an entity as a result of past events from which future economic benefits are expected to flow.

label: Asset tracking
plain_descriptions: monitoring the physical location and movement of valuable equipment and shipping containers
system using gps, bluetooth, or cellular tags to locate freight and warehouse inventory
summary: The method of tracking the geographical position, transit status, and physical condition of physical assets and cargo utilizing wireless positioning and telemetry technologies.

label: Async/await
plain_descriptions: syntax that lets developers write asynchronous, non-blocking code that reads like normal sequential instructions
language keywords used to pause execution until a background operation finishes without freezing the thread
summary: A syntactic abstraction that allows asynchronous, promise-based operations to be written and structured in a readable sequential style.

label: Attention mechanism
plain_descriptions: an AI technique that weighs which input words matter most at each step
the computational method letting models focus dynamically on relevant context
summary: A mathematical algorithm allowing neural models to calculate dynamic relevance weights between all tokens within an input sequence.

label: Reach
plain_descriptions: the number of unique individual people who see your content or ad
how many different people your message successfully touches
summary: The total number of distinct, unduplicated individuals or user accounts exposed to a piece of media content or advertisement during a specified period.

label: Authentication
plain_descriptions: verifying that a user or service matches their stated digital identity
checking user credentials such as passwords or biometrics to prove identity
summary: The security process of verifying the claimed identity of a user, device, or system.

label: Authorization
plain_descriptions: deciding what actions an identified user is allowed to perform
granting specific permissions to access protected resources
summary: The security process that determines whether an authenticated entity has permission to perform a requested operation or access a resource.

label: Autoscaling
plain_descriptions: automatically adding more servers when traffic spikes and removing them when things quiet down to save money
the system capability that expands or shrinks computing power based on real-time demand
summary: A cloud mechanism that automatically adjusts the number of active computing resources up or down based on real-time demand metrics.

label: Availability zone (AZ)
plain_descriptions: isolated data center location within a cloud region with its own power
discrete fault domain designed to keep systems running if another center fails
summary: One or more discrete physical data centers within a region with independent power, cooling, and networking designed for fault tolerance.

label: B-roll
plain_descriptions: secondary video footage cut into a scene to visually support the primary interview or narrative
background and illustrative camera shots used in film editing to cover cuts and enhance context
summary: Supplemental video footage spliced alongside primary interview or action shots to illustrate topics, hide edit splices, and enrich storytelling.

label: Backlink
plain_descriptions: a clickable link on another website that points back to yours
an external vote of confidence connecting another page to your site
summary: An incoming hyperlink from an external web domain directing users and web crawlers to a target page on another website.

label: Backpressure
plain_descriptions: signaling a fast sender to slow down so a slower receiver does not crash
mechanism where downstream consumers tell producers how much data they can accept
summary: A flow-control mechanism in asynchronous software pipelines where downstream consumers signal their capacity upstream to prevent producers from overwhelming them with data.

label: BACnet
plain_descriptions: open standard communications protocol designed specifically for commercial building automation systems
standardized networking language interconnecting heating, air conditioning, and lighting controllers in facilities
summary: A standardized communication protocol engineered specifically for building automation and control systems, facilitating multi-vendor interoperability across HVAC, lighting, and access control hardware.

label: Balance sheet
plain_descriptions: financial snapshot showing what a business owns and owes at one moment
document balancing company assets against debts and owner equity
summary: A core financial statement summarizing an entity’s assets, liabilities, and shareholders’ equity at a specific point in time.

label: Bandwidth
plain_descriptions: maximum amount of data that can travel through an internet connection per second
width of a network data highway measured in megabits or gigabits per second
summary: The maximum rate of data transfer across a given network communication path, typically measured in bits per second.

label: Bank transfer
plain_descriptions: electronic moving of money from one bank account directly into another
digital payment sent between bank accounts without physical cash or paper checks
summary: An electronic transfer of funds from one bank account to another across an interbank clearing and settlement network.

label: Batch processing
plain_descriptions: processing collected piles of business records all together at a scheduled time
running heavy calculation jobs overnight over yesterday's accumulated sales records
summary: The execution of a series of non-interactive computing jobs on large accumulated blocks of data without manual intervention.

label: Batch size
plain_descriptions: the number of training examples processed together in one forward and backward step
how many data samples an AI looks at before updating its internal weights
summary: The number of training samples processed simultaneously in a single iteration before the model parameters are updated.

label: Big O notation
plain_descriptions: mathematical shorthand describing how an algorithm’s runtime or memory demand grows as input size gets huge
metric that classifies algorithm efficiency by focusing on worst-case scaling behavior while ignoring hardware differences
summary: A mathematical notation used to describe the asymptotic upper bound of an algorithm’s time or memory requirements as the input size approaches infinity.

label: Binary search
plain_descriptions: fast search algorithm that finds an item in a sorted list by repeatedly dividing the search range in half
lookup technique that compares target values against the middle element of an ordered array
summary: An efficient search algorithm that finds the position of a target value within a sorted array by repeatedly halving the search interval.

label: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)
plain_descriptions: short range wireless personal area network technology designed for minimal battery drain
power efficient radio specification for exchanging sensor data with nearby devices
summary: A power-optimized wireless personal area network technology designed for short-range communication with minimal electrical energy consumption.

label: Block storage
plain_descriptions: raw virtual hard disk volume attached directly to a cloud virtual machine
high-speed storage split into fixed-size blocks for databases and operating systems
summary: A storage architecture that splits data into evenly sized raw blocks, exposed as virtual disk volumes attached to compute instances for high-speed I/O.

label: Blockchain
plain_descriptions: a shared digital record book where transactions are grouped into blocks and locked together cryptographically
a decentralized ledger maintained by a network of computers rather than a central server or bank
summary: A decentralized, tamper-resistant digital ledger of transactions recorded cryptographically in linked chronological blocks across a distributed network.

label: Blue-green deployment
plain_descriptions: running two identical environments side by side and switching user traffic instantly to the new one
a release technique that eliminates downtime by preparing updates in a cloned backup environment
summary: A deployment strategy that provisions two identical production environments (Blue and Green), shifting all traffic from the active to the idle environment upon validation.

label: Bond
plain_descriptions: loan you make to a government or corporation that pays you fixed interest and returns your money at maturity
fixed-income investment where an issuer promises regular interest payments and full principal repayment
summary: A fixed-income debt instrument issued by governments or corporations that pays periodic interest to bondholders and repays principal at maturity.

label: Yield
plain_descriptions: percentage return earned annually on a bond based on its current market price
effective interest rate generated by a bond investment over time
summary: The percentage rate of return generated on a bond or fixed-income investment relative to its purchase price or par value.

label: Bounce rate
plain_descriptions: the percentage of visitors who leave a website after viewing only one page
how often people immediately exit a site without interacting further
summary: A digital analytics metric quantifying the share of site visits lacking meaningful user engagement, where guests depart without triggering secondary actions.

label: Breaking change
plain_descriptions: a modification in software or an API that breaks existing programs depending on it
an update that requires downstream developers to rewrite parts of their code to keep working
summary: A modification in a software interface, dependency, or system component that breaks backward compatibility and necessitates code adjustments in dependent systems.

label: Breaking news
plain_descriptions: real-time reports on urgent events developing as we speak
immediate media updates about sudden occurrences of high public interest
summary: Newly received information about an urgent, ongoing event that warrants immediate public dissemination across news outlets.

label: Breakpoint
plain_descriptions: intentional pause point placed in code that halts program execution so developers can inspect state
marker set on a specific line of source code where a debugger suspends the running thread
summary: An intentional stopping point configured in source code or instruction addresses where a debugger suspends execution to allow state inspection.

label: Browser cache
plain_descriptions: a temporary storage folder where your browser saves images and files to reload sites faster
local memory holding downloaded web assets to avoid requesting them repeatedly
summary: A temporary storage mechanism within a web browser that retains previously fetched HTTP resources to speed up future requests.

label: Brute-force attack
plain_descriptions: systematically guessing every possible password until the correct one works
cracking a lock by trying every combination one by one at high speed
summary: An attack method that systematically checks all possible passwords, keys, or hashes until the correct combination is discovered.

label: Budget
plain_descriptions: plan for how much money to spend and save each month
roadmap tracking incoming paychecks against upcoming bills
summary: An itemised financial plan that estimates anticipated income and allocates it toward expenses, savings, and debt payoff over a set period.

label: Artifact
plain_descriptions: compiled files, binaries, or packages produced by a build pipeline for deployment or storage
tangible output file generated during compilation that can be tested, shared, or installed
summary: A file or collection of files produced by a build process that can be archived, distributed, or deployed to target environments.

label: Bundler
plain_descriptions: a development tool that packages hundreds of code files into clean web bundles
a build program that combines JavaScript modules, styles, and assets for fast browser loading
summary: A build tool that traverses project dependencies to combine and optimize multiple code and asset files into production-ready web bundles.

label: Burndown chart
plain_descriptions: visual graph showing remaining work decreasing day by day throughout a sprint
progress tracking chart comparing actual remaining effort against an ideal completion slope
summary: A graphical representation of work left to do versus time, utilized by agile squads to forecast sprint completion trajectories.

plain_descriptions: tools that turn raw corporate spreadsheets into visual performance reports
software that queries past sales and operational data to spot trends
summary: Strategies and software technologies used by enterprises to analyze historical business data and guide operational decision-making.

label: Byline
plain_descriptions: the line crediting the reporter who investigated and wrote the piece
attribution stating who authored a printed or online article
summary: A line in a publication identifying the writer or contributor responsible for the reporting and prose of an article.

label: Cache
plain_descriptions: a fast temporary storage area saving frequent answers so the computer skips slow re-calculations
keeping copies of popular web pages in memory so users don't wait for slow database queries
summary: A high-speed data storage layer that stores a subset of transient data so future requests are served faster than accessing primary storage.

label: Call to action (CTA)
plain_descriptions: a prompt or button telling a visitor exactly what step to take next
the direct invitation urging people to buy, sign up, or click now
summary: A marketing prompt, button, or statement designed to encourage immediate user response and guide prospects toward a desired action.

label: Callback
plain_descriptions: executable subroutine supplied as an input parameter to be triggered upon task conclusion
packaged piece of code passed to a recipient procedure to execute when a specific event happens
summary: A subroutine delivered as a parameter to another procedure to be called back upon the occurrence of a predefined trigger.

label: CAN bus
plain_descriptions: robust serial bus system allowing microcontrollers inside vehicles and machines to talk without a host computer
two-wire differential broadcast network engineered for electrical noise immunity in automotive and industrial machinery
summary: A robust, message-based broadcast bus standard designed to allow microcontrollers and electronic control units to communicate reliably in electrically harsh automotive and industrial environments.

label: Canary release
plain_descriptions: testing a new software version on a tiny percentage of real users before releasing it to everyone
a gradual rollout technique that exposes early bugs safely without risking the entire user base
summary: A deployment technique that exposes a new software release to a small fraction of production traffic to validate behavior before broader rollout.

label: CAP theorem
plain_descriptions: a fundamental rule stating distributed systems can only provide two out of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance
the reality that when cloud networks get cut, a database must choose between giving fresh answers or staying online
summary: A fundamental principle of distributed computing stating that a distributed data store can simultaneously provide at most two out of three guarantees, Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance.

label: Capacity planning
plain_descriptions: forecasting how much computing power and storage a business will need as user traffic increases
calculating server and network requirements in advance so infrastructure never runs out of resources
summary: The disciplined practice of estimating future computing demands to ensure sufficient infrastructure resources exist to support service growth.

label: Cash flow statement
plain_descriptions: document tracking hard currency entering and leaving corporate bank accounts
financial report breaking down cash changes into operating, investing, and financing
summary: A financial statement tracking the aggregate inflows and outflows of actual cash across operating, investing, and financing operations.

label: Content Delivery Network (CDN)

a distributed cache that speeds up websites by serving files from nearby edge servers
summary: A geographically distributed network of proxy servers that caches and delivers web content to users with low latency and high availability.

label: Certificate authority (CA)
plain_descriptions: a trusted organization that issues digital certificates to verify website and entity identities
the digital passport agency of the internet that signs certificates
summary: A trusted third-party organization that validates the identity of entities and issues cryptographically signed digital certificates.

label: Chain-of-thought prompting
plain_descriptions: asking the AI to think step by step
making the AI show its working before the answer
summary: A prompting technique that asks a model to reason through intermediate steps before it gives the final answer.

label: Change data capture (CDC)
plain_descriptions: identifying and tracking row changes in a database so other systems update automatically
watching the database transaction log to copy edits to search indexes and caches in real time
summary: A set of software design patterns and techniques used to capture and deliver row-level data modifications as they happen.

label: Chaos engineering
plain_descriptions: intentionally breaking parts of a live system to uncover weaknesses before outages happen
controlled experiments in production to test whether software survives unexpected hardware or network failures
summary: The systematic practice of injecting controlled turbulence into a software environment to assess its resilience under stress.

label: Chunking

splitting text files into bite-sized segments with overlap so language models can search them accurately
summary: The process of partitioning lengthy documents into smaller, cohesive textual segments to optimize semantic embedding density and retrieval precision in Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems.

label: Churn rate
plain_descriptions: percentage of customers who stop using or paying for a service during a given time period
rate at which subscribers cancel memberships or abandon an application
summary: The share of paying users who stop, by cancelling or not renewing, during a given period.

label: CI/CD

the automated pipeline that moves software from development to live production servers
summary: A modern engineering methodology uniting frequent source integration with automated regression testing and reliable application deployment.

label: Pipeline

the scripted sequence that takes software from a commit to a deployable artifact
summary: A defined sequential series of automated execution steps that compiles, tests, and packages application updates.

label: Circuit breaker
plain_descriptions: automatic switch stopping calls to failing services to prevent system crashes
safety mechanism tripping requests when remote dependencies become unresponsive
summary: A design pattern that prevents an application from repeatedly attempting an operation likely to fail, tripping to fail fast and recovering automatically when healthy.

label: Class
plain_descriptions: architectural template for manufacturing objects with shared attributes and behaviors
code blueprint specifying what variables and methods an instantiated entity will possess
summary: An extensible code template that defines the state properties and callable behaviors for constructing objects.

label: Classification
plain_descriptions: assigning data items into distinct categories such as determining if an email is spam or normal
machine learning tasks where the predicted outcome is a separate class label
summary: A supervised machine learning task where an algorithm predicts discrete qualitative class labels or category assignments for given input observations.

label: Clean architecture
plain_descriptions: layering software so business rules stay independent of frameworks and databases
code design where internal logic points inward and knows nothing about external tools
summary: A software architectural paradigm structured in concentric layers where dependencies point strictly inward toward domain logic, decoupling business rules from frameworks and databases.

label: Closure
plain_descriptions: function bundled together with references to its surrounding lexical environment
inner function that remembers and accesses variables from its enclosing scope even after that parent function has returned
summary: A function packaged with references to its surrounding lexical scope, enabling it to access enclosing variables even after the outer function finishes executing.

label: Instance
plain_descriptions: virtual server running in the cloud with assigned CPU and memory
rented cloud computer instance that you can start or stop on demand
summary: A virtual compute environment provisioned on cloud infrastructure with dedicated allocations of vCPUs, memory, and network capabilities.

label: Region
plain_descriptions: separate geographic location where cloud data centers are clustered
physical territory or city hosting isolated cloud infrastructure
summary: A distinct physical geographical area comprising multiple isolated and physically separated availability zones interconnected via private low-latency links.

label: Clustering
plain_descriptions: grouping similar data points together based on shared characteristics without pre-made tags
unsupervised partitioning of items into subsets that share close geometrical distances
summary: An unsupervised machine learning task that groups unlabelled observations into subsets whose member data points share higher similarity to one another than to points in other groups.

label: Content management system (CMS)
plain_descriptions: website platform for writing and publishing articles without code
admin dashboard where editors manage web pages and media assets
summary: Software that lets editors create, format, publish, and organize digital content on the web without editing source code directly.

label: Convolutional neural network (CNN)

machine learning architectures using sliding filter kernels to recognize visual patterns
summary: A deep learning architecture that utilizes convolutional layers with weight sharing and pooling mechanisms to extract spatial feature hierarchies from grid-structured data like images.

label: Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP)

lightweight http alternative designed to run restful requests on tiny microcontrollers
summary: A specialized RESTful web transfer protocol designed by the IETF for resource-constrained microcontrollers and low-power wireless networks using UDP.

label: Code review

a peer inspection of source code to catch bugs and uphold standards
summary: A collaborative peer-review practice where software engineers systematically examine proposed code changes to identify defects, enforce architectural standards, and share knowledge.

label: Code splitting

breaking up big JavaScript files so users do not download unnecessary code up front
summary: A technique of splitting a single application bundle into multiple smaller chunks that can be loaded on demand or in parallel.

label: Cold chain monitoring
plain_descriptions: continuous temperature and humidity surveillance of temperature-sensitive pharmaceuticals and perishable food during shipping
automated tracking system auditing refrigeration conditions inside cargo containers to prevent cargo spoilage
summary: The specialized technological process of continuously measuring, logging, and verifying ambient temperature and environmental conditions across the shipping, storage, and handling of temperature-sensitive goods.

label: Cold start
plain_descriptions: delay when a serverless function starts up from scratch after idle time
initial pause while the cloud provider spins up a new container for your code
summary: The initial invocation latency experienced in serverless computing when the platform must download code, initialize a container, and boot the runtime.

label: Color grading
plain_descriptions: stylized color adjustment enhancing emotional tone and artistic mood in videos and photographs
post-production color manipulation shaping the visual palette and atmosphere of footage
summary: The creative process in video post-production where color properties, tonal balances, and contrast curves are altered to produce an artistic mood or stylized look.

label: Columnar storage
plain_descriptions: organizing database records by columns instead of rows on disk
grouping all prices together on storage drives so summing sales skips reading customer names
summary: A database storage method where data blocks group values by column across records rather than by row, accelerating analytical aggregation queries.

label: Compiler
plain_descriptions: tool that translates entire source code files into machine code or bytecode before execution
program that analyzes human-readable code and converts it into a runnable standalone binary
summary: A computer program that translates software source code written in a high-level programming language into machine code or an intermediate representation prior to execution.

label: Compound Interest

money snowballing because earnings get added back to the pile
summary: Interest calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

label: Computer vision

summary: A domain of artificial intelligence that trains digital systems to identify, process, and derive meaningful insights from digital imagery, video feeds, and visual inputs.

label: Concurrency

software structure that interleaves or coordinates several computations without requiring them to run at the exact same physical instant
summary: The composition and coordination of multiple computational tasks executing over overlapping time intervals.

real-time health tracking of industrial motors and bearings to prevent unexpected machinery breakdowns
summary: The systematic, continuous monitoring of physical operating parameters—such as vibration, temperature, and acoustics—to identify mechanical changes indicative of developing faults.

label: Configuration management

keeping track of system configs using code so environments remain consistent and drift-free
summary: The automated discipline and toolset used to establish, track, and maintain consistency of system settings and software across infrastructure assets.

label: Confusion matrix
