a matrix comparing true actual labels against predicted model labels across all classes
summary: A specialized contingency table layout that visually summarizes classification model performance by cross-tabulating actual ground-truth labels against predicted outcomes.

label: Connection pool
plain_descriptions: a shared cache of open database connections ready for apps to use without reconnecting
keeping pre-warmed database lines open so web requests avoid slow network handshakes
summary: A cache of open, reusable database connection objects maintained so that applications avoid the high overhead of establishing new connections for each request.

label: Consistent hashing
plain_descriptions: hashing technique that minimizes data movement when servers are added or removed
distributed algorithm mapping keys and nodes onto a circular ring to prevent mass rebalancing
summary: A distributed hashing algorithm where resizing the bucket array requires only K/N keys to be remapped on average, mapping nodes and data keys onto a circular ring space.

label: Image
plain_descriptions: the static template or blueprint used to create and run containers
a frozen snapshot of software files, system libraries, and startup commands
summary: An immutable, read-only package containing application binaries, libraries, configuration files, and metadata required to launch a container.

label: Container registry
plain_descriptions: storage repository for publishing, sharing, and downloading container images
app store library where Docker images are stored and pulled by servers
summary: A centralized storage and content delivery system for storing, managing, and distributing container images across development and production environments.

label: Content marketing
plain_descriptions: creating helpful articles, videos, and guides to attract and keep customers
marketing by teaching and entertaining people rather than just pitching products
summary: A strategic marketing approach focused on creating and distributing valuable, relevant, and consistent content to attract and retain a clearly defined audience.

label: Context engineering
plain_descriptions: the practice of carefully designing and managing everything fed into an AI's context window
organizing tokens, instructions, tools, and history to maximize AI accuracy and reduce cost
summary: The disciplined practice of curating, structuring, compressing, and caching the information loaded into a model's context window to optimize performance and efficiency.

label: Context window
plain_descriptions: how much text the AI can keep in mind at once
the AI’s working memory limit
summary: The maximum amount of text, counted in tokens, that a model considers in one request, covering the prompt, the conversation so far and its reply.

label: Conversion rate
plain_descriptions: the percentage of website visitors who complete a desired action like buying or signing up
how successfully your web traffic turns into actual paying customers or leads
summary: The percentage of total visitors or interactions that culminate in the completion of a defined goal or desired transaction.

label: Cookie
plain_descriptions: small browser file websites save to remember your login
web tracker banner you click accept on
summary: A small piece of data stored on the user's browser by websites to retain state and track browsing activity.

label: Copyright
plain_descriptions: the legal right giving creators exclusive control over how their works are copied and shared
intellectual property protection preventing unauthorized reproduction of original creative works
summary: A form of intellectual property law protecting original works of authorship fixed in any tangible medium of expression from unauthorized copying and distribution.

label: Core Web Vitals
plain_descriptions: Google standards measuring how fast, responsive, and visually stable a website is
key performance scores that directly influence web page ranking and user experience
summary: A set of standardized metrics established by Google to evaluate real-world user experience across loading speed, responsiveness, and visual stability.

label: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)
plain_descriptions: a browser security check deciding if one website can fetch data from another domain
the rules preventing malicious websites from secretly querying your banking API
summary: A browser security protocol using special HTTP headers that lets an API grant specific foreign websites permission to fetch its content.

label: Cost per click (CPC)
plain_descriptions: the amount of money you pay each time a person clicks your ad
total ad cost divided by the number of clicks received
summary: An online advertising pricing model where the advertiser pays a fee each time a user clicks on one of their ads.

label: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
plain_descriptions: statistical basket tracking price changes for everyday goods bought by households
standard economic benchmark measuring the cost of living fluctuations
summary: A statistical index measuring the weighted average change over time in prices paid by households for a representative basket of consumer goods and services.

label: Cost per mille (CPM)
plain_descriptions: the price an advertiser pays for every one thousand times an ad is seen
ad cost calculated per batch of one thousand views
summary: An advertising pricing model where the buyer pays a predetermined rate for every one thousand impressions their ad receives.

label: Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)
plain_descriptions: separating data update logic from data reading logic into distinct models
architectural pattern using different models to write and read data
summary: An architectural pattern that separates operations that mutate state from operations that read data into distinct models and pipelines.

label: Creative Commons
plain_descriptions: standardized public licenses enabling creators to share works with flexible permissions
open copyright framework allowing free cultural reuse while reserving specific conditions
summary: A nonprofit organization and legal framework providing standardized copyright licenses that permit free public distribution and remixing of creative works under specified conditions.

label: Credit card
plain_descriptions: payment card that lets you buy things on credit up to a preset limit
plastic card allowing you to borrow money from a bank for purchases and pay later
summary: A payment card issued by a financial institution that enables cardholders to borrow funds up to an approved limit to make purchases or cash advances.

label: Credit score
plain_descriptions: three-digit number showing lenders the probability of repaying borrowed money on time
personal financial grade determining whether you get approved for loans and credit cards
summary: A numerical assessment calculated from credit history that indicates an individual's creditworthiness and likelihood of repaying debt obligations on time.

label: Crisis communication
plain_descriptions: messaging strategies used to protect reputation during unexpected emergencies
handling media and public briefings when an institution faces severe operational failure
summary: Strategic public communications deployed during emergencies to mitigate reputational damage, protect public safety, and convey truthful instructions.

label: Customer relationship management (CRM)
plain_descriptions: software that tracks customer interactions and deals
a shared database where sales and support log conversations
summary: A business system that organizes customer details, communications, and sales opportunities in one shared workspace.

label: Cryptocurrency
plain_descriptions: digital money that uses cryptography instead of a central bank to secure transactions and control creation
electronic currency exchanged directly between people on a decentralized computer network
summary: A digital or virtual currency that relies on cryptographic mechanisms for security and operates across a decentralized distributed ledger.

label: Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
plain_descriptions: an attack that tricks your browser into making unwanted money transfers on sites where you are logged in
clicking a trap link on an external page that secretly submits a form to change your account email
summary: An attack that tricks an authenticated web browser into sending unauthorized commands to a vulnerable web application without the user’s consent.

label: CSS
plain_descriptions: the code rules that control colors, fonts, and layouts on a website
the styling stylesheet language that makes web pages visually appealing
summary: A declarative styling language for rendering visual layout, typographic formatting, and color palettes on markup documents.

label: Click-through rate (CTR)
plain_descriptions: the percentage of people who click on your link after seeing it
clicks divided by impressions expressed as a percentage
summary: Clicks on an ad or link as a share of the times it was shown.

label: Customer lifetime value (CLV)
plain_descriptions: total amount of money a business expects to earn from a customer throughout their entire relationship
projected net profit or revenue generated by a single user account over its lifespan
summary: The projected total revenue or profit that a business anticipates earning from a single customer throughout the duration of their relationship.

label: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE)
plain_descriptions: the standardized global dictionary of publicly recognized cybersecurity flaws and software bugs
an official tracking code like CVE-2021-44228 identifying a specific security flaw
summary: A publicly available list of standardized identifiers for cybersecurity vulnerabilities and exposures.

label: Daily active users (DAU)
plain_descriptions: count of unique people who open and interact with an application in a single day
vital metric tracking daily user volume and ongoing product engagement
summary: The total count of unique individuals who initiate a meaningful interaction with a software application within a 24-hour day.

label: Daily Scrum
plain_descriptions: quick fifteen-minute daily morning meeting for developers to sync on sprint progress
brief stand-up check-in where teammates share achievements, plans, and immediate blockers
summary: A 15-minute daily inspect-and-adapt event for developers to synchronize activities and plan the next 24 hours of work.

label: Dashboard
plain_descriptions: single visual screen combining real-time gauges, graphs, and indicators about system health
centralized console displaying operational metrics so engineers can assess infrastructure status at a glance
summary: A visual interface that consolidates and presents real-time telemetry metrics and system statuses on a single screen for rapid operational evaluation.

label: Dynamic application security testing (DAST)
plain_descriptions: testing a running web application from the outside by sending simulated malicious requests
black-box security scanning that probes live applications for exploitable vulnerabilities
summary: A black-box testing methodology that assesses running applications from the outside by injecting fault payloads to detect runtime security vulnerabilities.

label: Data governance
plain_descriptions: the company rules and processes that ensure data stays secure, accurate, and properly used
managing who owns, controls, and has permission to access business records across an organization
summary: The overall management framework of data availability, usability, integrity, and security across an enterprise.

label: Data labeling
plain_descriptions: the process of tagging raw data like images or text with informative labels so algorithms can learn from them
adding ground-truth tags and annotations to training samples for supervised machine learning
summary: The operational process of identifying, annotating, and tagging raw data samples with informative target labels to produce ground-truth training datasets for supervised machine learning.

label: Data lake
plain_descriptions: a huge digital reservoir where companies store raw data in any format until needed
a flexible storage pool holding audio, text, images, and logs without forcing strict table structures
summary: A scalable storage repository designed to retain massive volumes of raw multi-format information without requiring an upfront database schema.

label: Data lakehouse
plain_descriptions: a modern data storage setup combining cheap file storage with fast database query tables
an architecture that lets companies run business reports and machine learning directly on raw data files
summary: A modern data management architecture that combines the cost-effective storage of data lakes with the ACID transactions of data warehouses.

label: Data lineage
plain_descriptions: tracing the full journey of information from where it was created to every final report
a visual family tree showing how raw database records get transformed along the way
summary: The recorded lifecycle and lifecycle path of data that documents its origin, movement, transformations, and destinations over time.

label: Data pipeline
plain_descriptions: an automated series of steps moving information from where it is created to where it is used
software plumbing that pumps live data from user clicks into analytics systems
summary: An automated sequence of processes that ingests, processes, and transfers raw data from source systems to destination storage.

label: Data quality
plain_descriptions: how reliable, clean, and complete a collection of records is for business use
checking that information is accurate, up to date, and free from duplicate entries
summary: The measurement of how well a dataset satisfies requirements for accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, and timeliness.

label: Data structure
plain_descriptions: organized layout for storing and managing information efficiently in computer memory
specialized format for grouping data items to optimize search, insertion, and retrieval operations
summary: A specialized format for organizing, processing, retrieving, and storing data efficiently within computer systems.

label: Data visualization
plain_descriptions: turning raw numbers into charts and graphs that people can understand
visual displays like heatmaps and line plots that show trends in data
summary: The practice of representing quantitative data graphically through charts, maps, and visual plots to communicate insights clearly.

label: Data warehouse
plain_descriptions: a central database designed specifically for business analysis and fast executive reporting
a giant organized filing room where companies store cleaned historical business records
summary: A centralized, relational repository that aggregates structured historical data from across an organization to power business intelligence and reporting.

label: Index
plain_descriptions: a sorted lookup helper that lets the database find specific rows in milliseconds instead of scanning the whole disk
an alphabetical index at the back of a book pointing directly to table rows
summary: A specialized data structure associated with a database table that accelerates record retrieval at the expense of extra storage and slower writes.

label: Migration
plain_descriptions: a version-controlled script that safely updates database table layouts as software evolves
a step-by-step code file for adding new columns or tables to live databases
summary: A version-controlled set of programmatic scripts that safely alter database schemas over time without losing existing data.

label: Normalization
plain_descriptions: organizing database tables to eliminate duplicate copies of the same information
structuring relational tables so every piece of data is stored in exactly one logical place
summary: The process of structuring a relational database in accordance with normal forms to reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity.

label: Replication
plain_descriptions: copying database records automatically to backup servers so the system survives hardware failures
syncing data across multiple database copies so heavy user reads don't slow down writes
summary: The continuous electronic copying of data from one database server to one or more replica servers to ensure high availability and read scalability.

label: Schema
plain_descriptions: the overall architectural blueprint defining the tables, columns, and rules in a database
the formal structural layout describing what kinds of data a database is allowed to hold
summary: The formal structural blueprint of a database that defines tables, fields, data types, relationships, and integrity constraints.

label: Transaction
plain_descriptions: an all-or-nothing group of database operations that either completely succeeds or leaves data untouched
a safe execution wrapper ensuring money transfers debit one account and credit another atomically
summary: A sequence of database operations executed as a single, atomic unit of work satisfying ACID properties.

label: Dataset
plain_descriptions: a structured collection of examples used to teach or test AI
the organized data gathered together for machine learning experiments
summary: A structured collection of data records, features, and targets partitioned to train, validate, and benchmark algorithms.

label: Distributed control system (DCS)
plain_descriptions: integrated industrial automation platform controlling complex continuous production plants across distributed controller nodes
plant-wide control architecture combining redundant controllers, databases, and operator stations into a unified network
summary: A centralized industrial control system architecture that utilizes decentralized autonomous controllers distributed throughout a plant to govern complex, continuous manufacturing processes.

label: Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS)
plain_descriptions: flooding a website with fake traffic from thousands of computers to knock it offline
overwhelming a server bandwidth so legitimate visitors cannot access the service
summary: A cyberattack that coordinates multiple distributed computers to flood a targeted server or network with traffic, rendering it inaccessible to legitimate users.

label: Deadlock
plain_descriptions: a freeze where two programs each wait forever for the resource held by the other
a traffic gridlock in database memory where transactions cannot move forward or release locks
summary: A permanent state of mutual blocking where two or more concurrent processes each hold a resource while waiting for another resource held by the other.

label: Debt-to-equity ratio (D/E)
plain_descriptions: proportion comparing how much a company borrows against how much shareholders own
financial leverage yardstick measuring debt dollars per dollar of net equity
summary: A financial leverage metric calculated by dividing an entity’s total debt obligations by its shareholders’ equity.

label: Debugging
plain_descriptions: investigative process of identifying, reproducing, and fixing defects in software
methodical workflow of diagnosing anomalous behavior using logs, assertions, and stepping tools
summary: The systematic engineering process of detecting, isolating, and rectifying software defects or anomalies.

label: Deep learning
plain_descriptions: machine learning powered by deep neural networks with many hidden layers
advanced AI techniques that automatically learn rich representations from raw data
summary: A specialized subset of machine learning utilizing multi-layered neural networks to extract hierarchical feature representations directly from complex data.

label: Definition of Done (DoD)
plain_descriptions: shared quality checklist that every piece of work must meet before being considered finished
formal agreement covering code reviews, automated tests, documentation, and deployment steps
summary: A formal commitment detailing the technical and quality standards that every product increment must satisfy to be release-ready.

label: Deflation
plain_descriptions: ongoing drop in general retail prices across an entire economy
economic condition where goods get cheaper but debts become harder to repay
summary: A persistent and widespread decline in the general price level of goods and services across an economy.

label: Dependency injection
plain_descriptions: passing required objects into a component from outside rather than creating them inside
supplying dependencies to a class via constructors or setters to improve testability
summary: A software design pattern where an object receives its dependencies from an external assembler rather than instantiating them internally, implementing inversion of control.

label: Deprecation
plain_descriptions: officially warning developers that a feature will be removed in a future update
marking old code as discouraged from use while keeping it working for now
summary: The practice of marking a software feature, API, or package as obsolete and discouraged from use, signaling that it will be removed in a future release.

label: Depreciation
plain_descriptions: spreading out the purchase cost of heavy equipment over the years it gets used
accounting write-down reflecting wear, tear, and aging of physical assets
summary: The systematic allocation of the depreciable cost of a tangible fixed asset over its estimated useful economic lifespan.

label: Design pattern
plain_descriptions: a reusable template or battle-tested solution to a commonly occurring coding problem
a proven blueprint for structuring software components to solve standard architectural challenges
summary: A named, proven way of structuring code that solves a design problem developers meet again and again, such as creating objects or reacting to changes.

label: Device provisioning
plain_descriptions: process of enrolling configuring and registering a new hardware unit into a cloud service
initial automated onboarding workflow that assigns credentials and configurations to devices
summary: The automated onboarding process that authenticates, registers, and configures newly deployed hardware devices into a centralized cloud management platform.

label: Device shadow
plain_descriptions: cloud-hosted digital document that stores and syncs the current and desired state of an iot device
virtual proxy that allows apps to send commands and read settings even when the device is offline
summary: A cloud-based virtual document that records, synchronizes, and persists the reported operational state and desired configuration of an IoT device across intermittent network connectivity.

label: DevOps
plain_descriptions: working culture and practices that unite software engineers and IT operations to ship updates faster
blending coding and system administration into automated pipelines that build, test, and release software smoothly
summary: A cultural philosophy, set of practices, and tools that combines software development and IT operations to shorten the development lifecycle and deliver high-quality software continuously.

label: Diffusion model
plain_descriptions: generative AI that creates crisp images by progressively cleaning up random visual noise
machine learning models that learn to reverse a gradual noise destruction process to synthesize pictures
summary: A class of generative neural networks trained to synthesize high-fidelity data, particularly images, by learning to iteratively reverse a progressive Markovian noise-diffusion process.

label: Digital signature
plain_descriptions: a mathematical stamp that proves who created a file and ensures it was not altered
an electronic seal providing proof of authorship and data integrity
summary: A mathematical scheme that binds an identity to digital data using asymmetric cryptography, providing authentication, data integrity, and non-repudiation.

label: Digital transformation
plain_descriptions: rewiring an entire business to operate using modern software and cloud tools
replacing paper forms and outdated legacy routines with digital services
summary: The strategic and cultural integration of digital technology across all areas of an organization to fundamentally modernize operations and deliver customer value.

label: Digital twin
plain_descriptions: virtual software counterpart of a physical asset updated with real time sensor metrics
computational model reflecting the live state behavior and lifecycle of real world machines
summary: A virtual representation that serves as the real-time computational counterpart of a physical object, process, or system synchronized through continuous telemetry.

label: Disaster recovery (DR)
plain_descriptions: plan and technical process to restore systems after a major outage or disaster
procedures for reviving critical business data and servers following regional catastrophes
summary: A coordinated set of policies, tools, and technical procedures designed to recover and resume mission-critical technology infrastructure and operations after a catastrophic event.

label: Distributed system
plain_descriptions: collection of independent computers working together appearing as a single system
software spread across multiple networked machines communicating to accomplish a task
summary: A system whose hardware and software components communicate and coordinate their actions over a network, presenting themselves to end users as a unified cohesive computing facility.

label: Distributed tracing
plain_descriptions: following a single user request as it travels across dozens of microservices to pinpoint where delays occur
a map showing the exact path and timing of an operation through connected servers
summary: A monitoring method that tracks the lifecycle of an execution request as it travels across multiple networked services and processes.

label: Diversification
plain_descriptions: spreading your investment money across many different assets so a loss in one will not wipe you out
the practice of not putting all your eggs into a single investment basket
summary: A risk-management technique that mixes a wide variety of investments within a portfolio to reduce unsystematic risk.

label: Dividend
plain_descriptions: portion of company profits distributed directly to shareholders
cash payout received per share for owning stock in a profitable company
summary: A distribution of a portion of a company's post-tax earnings decided by the board of directors and paid out to shareholders.

label: Domain Name System (DNS)
plain_descriptions: the internet phonebook that translates human-friendly website names like example.com into computer IP addresses
the directory service connecting domain names to web server numbers
summary: The hierarchical, decentralized naming system that translates human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses for network routing.

label: Docker
plain_descriptions: the most popular software tool for building, running, and managing containers
the platform that popularised container packaging for modern software development
summary: An open commercial platform providing tooling to build, share, package, and execute application containers using host operating system virtualization.

label: Docker Compose
plain_descriptions: coordinating interconnected microservice containers from a single project file
easy way to spin up a web app, database, and cache together using docker-compose.yml
summary: An orchestration utility that launches and connects groups of containerized application services using centralized declarative YAML specifications.

label: Document database
plain_descriptions: a database that stores records as self-contained JSON-like digital files
a flexible system where customer records hold their own nested lists without joining tables
summary: A specialized NoSQL database architecture built to store, retrieve, and manage semi-structured data formatted as documents like JSON or BSON.

label: Document Object Model (DOM)
plain_descriptions: the internal tree structure of a webpage that scripts can read and change
the programming interface representing webpage elements as interactive objects
summary: A cross-platform, language-independent programming interface that treats an HTML or XML document as a tree structure of nodes.

label: Domain-driven design (DDD)
plain_descriptions: software design methodology centering code around business models and shared language
structuring complex enterprise software according to real-world domain rules
summary: A software architectural methodology centering system design and implementation around core business models, ubiquitous language, and bounded contexts.

label: Double-entry bookkeeping
plain_descriptions: accounting rule requiring every single financial transaction to be recorded in at least two accounts
system matching debits against credits to keep financial balance sheets in equilibrium
summary: The universal bookkeeping method wherein every economic transaction is recorded in at least two separate ledger accounts with offsetting debit and credit entries.

label: DTLS
plain_descriptions: security protocol providing encrypted communications over datagram networks like udp
cryptographic wrapper protecting datagram transfers against packet tampering and eavesdropping
summary: A cryptographic security protocol based on TLS that provides confidentiality, message integrity, and authentication for datagram-based network communications.

label: E-commerce platform
plain_descriptions: software engine that runs web stores with shopping carts and inventory
online storefront software where merchants list items and process orders
summary: A comprehensive software suite that enables businesses to build online stores, showcase product catalogs, manage shopping carts, and fulfill digital orders.

label: E-wallet
plain_descriptions: smartphone app that stores payment details to pay for things online or in stores
electronic account holding stored balance or linked cards for contactless and online checkouts
summary: An electronic application or device that securely stores digital payment credentials and funds to facilitate online, in-app, and contactless transactions.

label: EBITDA
plain_descriptions: profit gauge ignoring interest payments, tax bills, and asset wear and tear
operational cash earnings metric stripping out financing and accounting choices
summary: An earnings metric measuring core operating profitability before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization deductions.

label: Edge AI
plain_descriptions: running artificial intelligence models locally on devices without sending raw data to remote servers
executing neural network inferences directly on microchips attached to cameras and sensors
summary: The execution of artificial intelligence algorithms and deep learning models directly on physical edge hardware without dependency on cloud infrastructure.

label: Edge case
plain_descriptions: an unusual or extreme scenario that occurs only at the outer limits of operating parameters
a rare condition or extreme input that software must handle without failing
summary: A problem or operational situation that occurs only at extreme minimum or maximum operating parameters, testing the boundaries of system resilience.

label: Edge computing
plain_descriptions: computing paradigm that analyzes and processes information near the data source location
decentralized framework running analytics directly on local hardware instead of remote servers
summary: A distributed computing paradigm that brings computational logic and data storage closer to the physical devices and sensors where information is generated.

label: Elasticsearch
plain_descriptions: a fast search and analytics engine that combs through millions of documents in seconds
software built to search articles by keywords, filter store catalogs, and monitor server log errors
summary: A distributed, JSON-based search and analytics engine built on Apache Lucene, designed for horizontal scalability, reliability, and real-time search.

label: Open rate
plain_descriptions: the percentage of delivered emails that recipients actually open to read
how many people out of your subscriber list clicked to open your message
summary: The percentage of successfully delivered emails opened by subscribers, indicating subject line effectiveness and audience engagement.

label: Embedded system
plain_descriptions: specialized computer built inside a larger machine to run dedicated tasks
compact microprocessor hardware dedicated entirely to single-purpose equipment control
summary: A dedicated computing assembly combining a microprocessor, firmware, and peripheral interfaces engineered to execute predefined control operations within an encompassing machine.

label: Embedding
plain_descriptions: turning words into a list of numbers so a computer can compare meanings
numbers that place similar ideas close together
summary: A list of numbers learned by a model to represent an item such as a word or a document, so that similar items end up close together.

label: Emergency fund
plain_descriptions: cash set aside to cover unexpected life emergencies without borrowing
safety net of three to six months of living expenses kept in a bank
summary: A liquid cash reserve maintained specifically to absorb unforeseen expenses or income disruptions without taking on debt or liquidating long-term investments.

label: Encryption
plain_descriptions: scrambling secret information into unreadable code that only someone with the correct key can unlock
locking confidential data with a digital key so eavesdroppers see only scrambled nonsense
summary: The cryptographic process of encoding plaintext into ciphertext so that only authorized parties with the matching decryption key can read it.

label: End-to-end encryption (E2EE)
plain_descriptions: encrypting messages so only the sender and receiver can read them, locking out servers in between
private communication where even the messaging company cannot see the plaintext
summary: A secure communication system where data is encrypted on the sender's device and decrypted only by the intended recipient, preventing intermediate parties from accessing the content.

label: End-to-end test
plain_descriptions: simulating a complete real user journey through the entire application from start to finish
testing an entire system including frontend, backend, database, and third-party integrations together
summary: A comprehensive testing methodology that validates the flow of an application from the user interface down through all underlying backend services and databases.

label: Energy harvesting
plain_descriptions: capturing ambient energy from light, heat, or vibrations to power electronics without batteries
technology that scavenges electricity from the environment for maintenance-free sensors
summary: The process of capturing minute quantities of energy from ambient environmental sources—such as light, thermal gradients, mechanical vibrations, or radio waves—and converting it into electrical power for electronics.

label: Engagement rate
plain_descriptions: the percentage of people who actively react, comment, or interact with your content
how enthusiastically an audience participates rather than just passively watching
summary: A performance metric that quantifies the level of active user interaction generated by content relative to its total reach, impressions, or followers.

label: Environment variable
plain_descriptions: a dynamic key-value setting stored outside software code to configure how it behaves in different environments
a configuration variable provided by the operating system to running programs
summary: A dynamic key-value pair stored in the operating system environment that configures program behavior without altering application source code.

label: Epic
plain_descriptions: large body of work that spans multiple sprints and is split into several user stories
major product initiative or feature theme organized across a longer development timeframe
summary: A substantial strategic initiative in agile software delivery that encompasses a collection of related user stories delivered over several sprints.

label: Epoch
plain_descriptions: one complete pass of an entire training dataset through an AI model
a full cycle of training where every single example has been seen once
summary: One complete training cycle during which the learning algorithm processes every sample in the training dataset exactly once.

label: Equity
plain_descriptions: value left for owners after paying off all business liabilities
total stake held by shareholders including contributed capital and accumulated profits
summary: The residual economic interest in an entity’s assets after deducting all of its liabilities.

label: Enterprise resource planning (ERP)
plain_descriptions: master software that runs company finances and inventory
central operational spine connecting accounting and warehouse data
summary: An integrated suite of core business applications that synchronizes finance, purchasing, inventory, and production across an organization.

label: Error budget
plain_descriptions: allowed amount of downtime or failed requests a service can have before engineers must freeze new releases
the mathematical cushion between 100% perfection and an agreed reliability objective
summary: The maximum acceptable amount of service unreliability or downtime permitted by a Service Level Objective during a given time window.

label: eSIM
plain_descriptions: programmable microchip soldered inside devices replacing physical removable telecom cards
embedded secure hardware module enabling remote carrier subscription provisioning
summary: A tamper-resistant integrated secure element soldered onto circuit boards that allows remote over-the-air provisioning of mobile carrier profiles without physical card swaps.

label: ESP32
plain_descriptions: powerful, low-cost microchip with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth for connected devices
dual-core microcontroller chip engineered specifically for wireless IoT gadgets
summary: A low-cost, low-power system on a chip microcontroller series featuring integrated Wi-Fi and dual-mode Bluetooth designed for wireless IoT product engineering.

label: Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF)
plain_descriptions: an investment fund traded on a stock exchange like an individual stock throughout the trading day
a basket of securities that you can buy and sell instantly with fluctuating market prices
summary: An investment fund traded directly on securities exchanges that holds a portfolio of assets designed to track an underlying index or sector.

label: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL)
plain_descriptions: pulling data from various places, cleaning it up, and saving it into a central analytics database
the three-step data pipeline that prepares raw business numbers for dashboards and reports
summary: A data integration process that extracts data from multiple sources, transforms it to meet analytical requirements, and loads it into a destination store.

label: Event-driven architecture
plain_descriptions: system architecture where decoupled services communicate by publishing and consuming events
software design reacting to state changes instead of making synchronous direct calls
summary: A software architecture paradigm where decoupled components communicate asynchronously by generating, detecting, and reacting to significant state changes known as events.

label: Event sourcing
plain_descriptions: storing every change to application state as an append-only sequence of immutable events
tracking full history like an accounting ledger rather than only keeping current values
summary: A persistence design pattern where all state changes are stored as an append-only, ordered sequence of immutable domain events instead of overwriting current entity records.

label: Event streaming
plain_descriptions: continuously capturing and processing digital records the moment an action happens
flowing operational updates across software applications without waiting for night-time file exports
summary: The practice of capturing, storing, and analyzing continuous flows of data records in real time as events occur.

label: Eventual consistency
plain_descriptions: a promise that all database copies will match eventually if no new edits are made
a design where your friend might see your social post a few seconds after you hit publish
summary: A consistency model used in distributed computing where all replicas of a data item will eventually converge to the same value given sufficient time without new updates.

label: Exception
plain_descriptions: unexpected event or runtime failure that interrupts the normal sequence of instructions
error signaling mechanism that transfers control up the call stack to a recovery block
summary: An abnormal condition or error event encountered during execution that disrupts normal instruction flow and triggers specialized handling logic.

label: Exchange rate
plain_descriptions: relative price tag determining how much foreign currency you get for one unit of domestic money
conversion value used when exchanging one nation’s currency for another
summary: The comparative price of one national currency expressed in terms of another currency.

label: Exponential backoff
plain_descriptions: waiting progressively longer between retries when an operation fails
retry strategy that doubles the sleep interval after each successive error
summary: An algorithm that progressively multiplies the delay interval between successive retries to prevent overwhelming struggling network services.

label: F1 score
plain_descriptions: a single combined score balancing precision and recall into a harmonic average
a reliable accuracy metric especially useful when dataset classes are heavily imbalanced
summary: A statistical evaluation metric that calculates the harmonic mean of precision and recall to provide a balanced measure of a classifier’s accuracy.

label: Fact-checking
plain_descriptions: verifying that claims, quotes, and statistics match verifiable evidence
investigating whether statements made by politicians and public figures are truthful
summary: The disciplined verification process of assessing factual assertions in published text, speeches, or broadcast reports against reliable primary documentation.

label: Failover
plain_descriptions: automatically switching to a backup server when the main server crashes
seamless transfer of traffic to redundant resources upon primary failure
summary: An operational procedure that automatically or manually redirects processing tasks and network traffic to a redundant standby system upon failure of the primary component.

label: Fair use
plain_descriptions: legal exception allowing limited quotation of copyrighted material for review or teaching
rule permitting unlicensed use of creative works for criticism, parody, or news reporting
summary: A legal doctrine permitting limited quotation and borrowing of copyrighted works without permission for purposes such as criticism, news reporting, teaching, or scholarship.

label: Feature engineering
plain_descriptions: transforming raw collected data into informative numerical inputs that machine learning models understand
crafting domain-specific predictive variables to boost the accuracy of an algorithm
summary: The machine learning practice of selecting, manipulating, and transforming raw dataset attributes into optimized feature representations to maximize algorithm performance.

label: Feature flag
plain_descriptions: a software switch that turns a feature on or off without deploying new code
a configuration toggle allowing gradual rollout of features to specific users
summary: A software engineering technique that enables or disables functionality remotely at runtime through configuration without altering and redeploying source code.

label: Few-shot prompting
plain_descriptions: showing the AI a few examples before asking
teaching by examples inside the question
summary: A prompting technique that includes a few worked examples of the task so the model follows the same pattern.

label: Fine-tuning
plain_descriptions: training an existing AI a bit more on your own examples
teaching a ready-made model a specialised job
summary: Further training of a pre-trained model on a smaller task-specific dataset so it performs better on that task or style.

label: FinOps

software analysis of written sentences, vocabulary, and linguistic intent

summary: A linear collection following the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) access discipline, restricting insertions and deletions to a single endpoint.

label: Stack trace
plain_descriptions: report showing the active sequence of function calls at the moment an error occurred
diagnostic breadcrumb trail of source files and line numbers where a program crashed
summary: A diagnostic report detailing the active call stack frames, function names, and file line numbers at a specific moment during execution.

label: Staging environment
plain_descriptions: a private test replica of the live website used for final quality checks before public release
the pre-production sandbox where software is tested under near-identical production conditions
summary: A pre-production testing environment that mirrors the exact hardware, architecture, and configuration of the production system to conduct final verification.

label: Stakeholder
plain_descriptions: anyone who has an interest in, influences, or is affected by the outcome of a product
key parties connected to a project, including end users, business leaders, investors, and regulatory bodies
summary: An individual, team, or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a product decision or outcome.

label: Pre-money valuation
plain_descriptions: agreed worth of a startup immediately before fresh investment cash is added
baseline company price tag determining equity dilution in a financing round
summary: The agreed valuation of a private enterprise determined prior to receiving an external injection of new investment capital.

label: Static site generation (SSG)
plain_descriptions: pre-building every page of a website into ready files before visitors arrive
generating fixed HTML pages during development for ultra-fast CDN delivery
summary: A build method that pre-renders full HTML pages at compile time rather than on demand for each user request.

label: Stock
plain_descriptions: unit of fractional ownership in a corporation that gives you a claim on its assets and profits
investment security representing a share of a company that trades on financial markets
summary: An equity security that represents fractional ownership in a corporation and entitles the stockholder to proportionate claims on earnings and voting rights.

label: Stock exchange
plain_descriptions: regulated marketplace where buyers and sellers trade corporate stocks and other securities
organized financial exchange matching bids and asks for shares of public companies
summary: An organized, regulated marketplace where securities such as stocks, bonds, and exchange-traded funds are bought and sold under standardized rules.

label: Story point
plain_descriptions: abstract measurement unit used to estimate the relative effort, complexity, and risk of a software task
scoring system that rates user story difficulty using relative comparisons rather than calendar hours
summary: A relative number that agile teams use to estimate how much total effort a backlog item will take, compared with other items.

label: Storyboard
plain_descriptions: visual sequence of illustrated panels sketching camera angles and action for a video shoot
drawn comic-strip plan showing how a commercial, animation, or movie scene will unfold
summary: A sequential visual layout of illustrations and annotations representing proposed camera angles, character movements, and staging before production begins.

label: Stream processing
plain_descriptions: analyzing and calculating data on the fly as individual pieces arrive
computing live business statistics continuously without stopping to bundle files
summary: The continuous ingestion and real-time computation of data records directly as they are generated.

label: Structured output
plain_descriptions: making the AI reply in an exact data format
getting JSON back instead of free text
summary: Model output constrained to follow a given format, usually a JSON schema, so that software can read it reliably.

label: Subagent
plain_descriptions: a specialized helper AI spawned by a main agent to handle a specific subtask
a secondary AI assistant focused on one piece of a larger project
summary: A specialized agent spawned and coordinated by a primary supervisor agent to execute an isolated, narrow task within a multi-agent system.

label: Subnet
plain_descriptions: smaller segmented portion of a larger IP network range
dividing a big network into isolated zones for security and organization
summary: A logical subdivision of an IP network designed to segment broadcast domains, improve routing efficiency, and enforce security boundaries.

label: Supervised learning
plain_descriptions: training a computer model using examples that already have the correct answers attached
machine learning where the algorithm learns from paired input features and target labels
summary: A machine learning approach where an algorithm learns a mapping function from input features to target outputs using training data composed of verified input-label pairs.

label: Supply chain attack
plain_descriptions: compromising an upstream software vendor or code library to infect downstream customers
sneaking malicious code into a trusted software update or package repository
summary: A cyberattack that targets less secure third-party vendors, libraries, or build pipelines to infiltrate the target organization's systems.

label: Synthetic data
plain_descriptions: artificially manufactured information generated by computer algorithms rather than collected from real people
simulated datasets created by models to train AI without compromising private personal records
summary: Algorithmically manufactured information engineered by mathematical models or computer simulations to replicate authentic dataset patterns without containing private personal records.

label: System prompt
plain_descriptions: hidden instructions an app gives the AI before you start chatting
the rules that set an assistant’s role and tone
summary: Instructions placed before the conversation that set the model’s role, rules and style for every later message.

label: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
plain_descriptions: reliable networking protocol that guarantees all data arrives completely and in order
connection-oriented rulebook ensuring web pages and files download without missing parts
summary: A connection-oriented transport layer protocol that provides reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of a stream of data packets.

label: Technical debt
plain_descriptions: the future cost of choosing a quick and dirty coding shortcut today
implied rework created when speedy software delivery sacrifices clean architecture
summary: The accumulated implied cost of additional future rework caused by choosing an expedited, suboptimal technical solution instead of a well-architected approach.

label: Telematics
plain_descriptions: combining telecommunications and vehicular informatics to monitor driving behavior and automobile diagnostics remotely
in-vehicle black box system sending speed, fuel consumption, and engine fault codes to fleet managers
summary: The interdisciplinary field combining telecommunications, vehicular technologies, and informatics to transmit real-time automotive telemetry, driving dynamics, and diagnostic data to remote backends.

label: Telemetry
plain_descriptions: automated collection and remote transmission of sensor measurements to a monitoring station
continuous stream of operational readings emitted by field hardware across a network
summary: The automated process of collecting operational metrics and status measurements from remote points and transmitting them across communications channels for monitoring and analysis.

label: Temperature
plain_descriptions: an AI setting that controls how creative or predictable generated text will be
a dial adjusting randomness in model answers from strictly factual to imaginative
summary: A sampling hyperparameter that scales logits before softmax to regulate the randomness and diversity of a language model's output tokens.

label: Term deposit
plain_descriptions: money locked in a bank for a set timeframe to earn a guaranteed higher interest rate
fixed-term bank deposit where early withdrawal triggers a penalty fee
summary: A fixed-term bank deposit that pays a predetermined rate of interest until a specified maturity date, imposing penalties for early withdrawal.

label: Terraform
plain_descriptions: tool for creating and managing cloud servers using readable code files
infrastructure as code software that provisions resources on multiple clouds
summary: An open-source infrastructure as code software tool that enables operators to provision and version multi-cloud data center resources using declarative configuration files.

label: Thread
plain_descriptions: secure, self-healing wireless mesh networking standard designed for smart home gadgets
IPv6-based mesh radio protocol that lets home devices talk to each other without single failure points
summary: An IPv6-based, low-power wireless mesh networking protocol built on IEEE 802.15.4 that provides reliable, secure, and self-healing connectivity for smart home devices without requiring a central hub.

label: Thread
plain_descriptions: smallest sequence of programmed instructions that an operating system scheduler can manage independently
lightweight execution line running inside a process that shares memory with sibling threads
summary: The smallest unit of execution within an operating system process, sharing its parent memory space and resources with other threads.

label: Threat modeling
plain_descriptions: analyzing a software design to brainstorm how an attacker might exploit it
a structured exercise to identify security risks and design mitigations early
summary: A structured engineering practice for identifying, categorizing, and prioritizing potential security threats to an application or system architecture.

label: Throughput
plain_descriptions: the total amount of work or data a computer system can process in one second
the volume of web requests or megabytes moving through a service over time
summary: The rate at which a computer system, communication channel, or application successfully processes and delivers data or transactions per unit of time.

label: Time-series database
plain_descriptions: a database designed specifically to track measurements changing over seconds, hours, and days
specialized software built for continuous sensor readings, stock ticks, and computer CPU graphs
summary: A database optimized for storing, querying, and analyzing sequences of data points indexed in chronological order.

label: TinyML
plain_descriptions: running artificial intelligence models directly on tiny, low-power microcontrollers
smart machine learning algorithms optimized to execute inside microchips using milliwatts of power
summary: A subfield of machine learning focused on optimizing and executing neural network models directly on resource-constrained microcontrollers operating in the milliwatt or microwatt power envelope.

label: Transport Layer Security (TLS)
plain_descriptions: the security protocol that powers the padlock icon and https in your browser address bar
an encrypted communications tunnel protecting internet traffic from eavesdropping and tampering
summary: A cryptographic communication protocol that provides privacy, data integrity, and authentication for communications over computer networks.

label: Certificate
plain_descriptions: a digital identity document that proves a website owns its public key and domain name
the security credential that enables the padlock icon and HTTPS encryption in browsers
summary: A digitally signed data file conforming to X.509 standards that binds a public key to an entity's domain name or identity.

label: Toil
plain_descriptions: repetitive, manual operational tasks that grow directly with service size and produce no lasting value
tedious administrative work like resetting servers or approving tickets that should be automated away by code
summary: Administrative operational effort within SRE comprising routine, automatable tasks that lack permanent architectural value and expand as fleet size increases.

label: Token
plain_descriptions: digital access pass sent with web requests
encoded string proving you are logged in
summary: A cryptographically signed string presented to servers to prove identity and authorization permissions.

label: Token
plain_descriptions: digital asset issued on an existing blockchain
utility or governance coin within a decentralized app
summary: A digital unit of value issued on top of an existing smart contract blockchain platform.

label: Token
plain_descriptions: unit AI uses to count text chunks
why AI charges per prompt length
summary: Small chunk of text, typically subword units, processed by large language models.

label: Tokenizer
plain_descriptions: the part that chops text into pieces the AI can read
what decides how many tokens a sentence costs
summary: The component that splits input such as text into tokens from a fixed vocabulary and turns them into numeric ids for the model.

label: Top-p sampling
plain_descriptions: picking next AI words only from the most probable group that adds up to p
an AI text sampling rule that cuts off unlikely, bizarre words dynamically
summary: A text generation decoding strategy that selects from the smallest subset of candidate tokens whose cumulative probability reaches a threshold p.

label: Transfer learning
plain_descriptions: taking a model trained on a huge general dataset and repurposing it for a specific new task
reusing learned weights and feature representations to train a new AI model with far less data
summary: A machine learning method where representations and weights learned from a broad primary task are adapted to solve a related target task with substantially reduced training data and computational overhead.

label: Transformer
plain_descriptions: the neural network design that powers modern large language models
an architecture that connects words across entire passages at once using self-attention
summary: A neural network architecture relying on self-attention mechanisms to process sequence elements in parallel without recurrent connections.

label: Tree shaking
plain_descriptions: removing unused pieces of code from final program files to save download size
an optimization step that strips away unreferenced functions and variables
summary: A dead-code elimination technique commonly used in modern JavaScript bundlers to remove unused exports from final production bundles.

label: Trunk-based development
plain_descriptions: branching practice where all developers merge small changes frequently into a single central branch
workflow that eliminates long-lived feature branches by integrating code directly to main every day
summary: A version control management practice where developers merge frequent, small code updates into a core branch called the trunk.

label: Type checking
plain_descriptions: verifying that variables and function arguments hold the expected kinds of data
catching mismatched data types before or during program execution
summary: The verification process that evaluates whether data values assigned to variables or passed to functions comply with the rules of a programming language type system.

label: TypeScript
plain_descriptions: a version of JavaScript that checks data types to prevent coding bugs
a typed superset of JavaScript that compiles down to plain JavaScript
summary: A strongly typed programming language that builds on JavaScript, giving developers better tooling and early error detection.

label: Typography
plain_descriptions: the craft of arranging fonts and text layout to make printed or digital words legible and appealing
artistic styling and formatting of letterforms across page and screen compositions
summary: The art, craft, and technique of selecting and arranging typefaces, font weights, kerning, and spacing to render written language legible, readable, and visually engaging.

label: UART
plain_descriptions: two-wire hardware circuit that sends and receives data character by character without a shared clock
asynchronous serial communication module commonly used for terminal logs and debugging
summary: A physical integrated circuit hardware block that translates parallel computing data into sequential asynchronous serial bitstreams over paired transmit (TX) and receive (RX) wires.

label: User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
plain_descriptions: fast lightweight network protocol that sends data without checking if it arrived
connectionless protocol used for real-time gaming, video streaming, and DNS
summary: A connectionless transport layer protocol that transmits data packets without prior connection handshakes or delivery guarantees, prioritizing speed over reliability.

label: Underfitting
plain_descriptions: when a machine learning model is too simplistic to capture the basic trends in its training data
a model performing poorly on both its training examples and new unseen test data
summary: A modeling pathology where a machine learning algorithm is overly simplistic, failing to capture the underlying structure of the data and exhibiting high loss on both training and test sets.

label: Unit test
plain_descriptions: an automated check testing the smallest single piece of code in isolation
verifying that an individual function returns the correct answer for given inputs
summary: An automated test that isolates and verifies the behavioral correctness of the smallest testable component or function of an application.

label: Unsupervised learning
plain_descriptions: machine learning that finds hidden patterns in data without pre-assigned labels or answers
algorithms grouping raw data points based on natural similarities without human guidance
summary: A category of machine learning where algorithms analyze and group unlabeled data to uncover underlying geometric clusters, manifold distributions, and intrinsic structures.

label: Uptime
plain_descriptions: the percentage of time a computer system or website is running and ready for users
how long a service stays available without crashing or going offline
summary: The proportion or duration of time that a computer system, network, or application remains fully functional and accessible to users.

label: URL
plain_descriptions: the complete address you type into a browser to visit a webpage
the standardized reference string locating internet documents and resources
summary: A structured reference syntax identifying network location coordinates and retrieval protocols for internet resources.

label: User story
plain_descriptions: short informal description of a software feature framed from the perspective of an end user
practical work item explaining who needs a capability, what they need, and why it provides value
summary: A concise, non-technical explanation of a software requirement capturing user intent, desired functionality, and business value.

label: UTM parameters
plain_descriptions: extra text tags added to the end of a web link to track where visitors came from
snippets of code in a URL showing which specific ad or post generated a click
summary: Five standardized query parameters appended to URLs that allow analytics platforms to track the source, medium, and campaign details of inbound web traffic.

label: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X)
plain_descriptions: communication system allowing vehicles to exchange safety data directly with other cars, pedestrians, and traffic lights
connected vehicle radio network transmitting collision warnings and intersection signal timing in milliseconds
summary: A vehicular communication technology suite facilitating direct, low-latency information exchange between a vehicle and its surrounding environment, including other vehicles, roadside infrastructure, pedestrians, and networks.

label: Variable
plain_descriptions: named container that holds data in memory while a program runs
symbolic label pointing to a value that can be read or modified
summary: A named storage location in memory paired with an identifier that holds data a program can manipulate.

label: Value-Added Tax (VAT)
plain_descriptions: consumption tax added at each stage of manufacturing and distribution
sales tax fractionally collected by businesses but borne by retail shoppers
summary: A multi-stage consumption tax levied on the incremental value added to goods and services across each stage of production and distribution.

label: Vector database
plain_descriptions: a database that finds things by similar meaning
storage that searches by how close lists of numbers are
summary: A database built to store embedding vectors and quickly return the ones most similar to a query vector.

label: Velocity
plain_descriptions: average amount of work a development team delivers during a single sprint
historical metric measuring how many story points a squad completes per iteration
summary: A planning metric tracking the average volume of story points or backlog items completed by a team per sprint.

label: Venture capital (VC)
plain_descriptions: professional investment money backing risky young startups in exchange for shares
funding ecosystem helping innovative high-growth ideas scale rapidly
summary: A specialized form of private equity financing provided by investment funds to early-stage startups with exceptional growth potential.

label: Vertical scaling
plain_descriptions: upgrading an existing server with more CPU, memory, or storage power
boosting capacity by replacing a machine with a larger hardware specification
summary: The practice of increasing system capacity by provisioning more compute resources, such as CPU cores, RAM, or storage speed, to a single server instance.

label: Virtual machine (VM)
plain_descriptions: a software simulation of an entire physical computer running its own complete operating system
a virtual computer created inside a powerful server that behaves just like a physical machine
summary: A software emulation of a physical computer system that executes applications within a dedicated, isolated guest operating system managed by a hypervisor.

label: Visual hierarchy
plain_descriptions: the layout principle organizing design elements in order of visual importance
arranging scale, color, and placement so viewers intuitively spot the most crucial information first
summary: The strategic arrangement and presentation of graphic design elements in deliberate order of importance, guiding the viewer's eye across the layout seamlessly.

label: Voice-over
plain_descriptions: off-screen spoken audio narrating or explaining visual actions in a video or documentary
vocal recording heard by viewers where the speaker does not appear directly on screen
summary: A production technique where an unseen narrator's spoken commentary is recorded and played over accompanying visual material or broadcast segments.

label: Volatility
plain_descriptions: how rapidly and dramatically an investment's price swings up and down over a period of time
a measure of how bumpy the financial ride is for a stock or asset
summary: A statistical measure of the dispersion of returns for a given security or market index over a specified timeframe.

label: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
plain_descriptions: isolated private network section inside a public cloud provider
virtual boundary that protects your cloud servers from public internet access
summary: A logically isolated virtual network dedicated to a cloud account, providing complete control over IP address ranges, subnets, and routing tables.

label: Virtual Private Network (VPN)
plain_descriptions: encrypted connection tunnel between your computer and a remote private network
secure way for employees to access internal company systems from home
summary: An encrypted communication channel constructed over a public network infrastructure to provide secure remote access and private site-to-site connectivity.

label: Web application firewall (WAF)
plain_descriptions: a protective shield that filters out malicious web traffic before it reaches your web server
an application-level firewall that blocks SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and bot spam
summary: A specialized security appliance or cloud filter that monitors, inspects, and blocks malicious HTTP and HTTPS traffic targeting web applications.

label: WCAG
plain_descriptions: the international official rulebook for digital accessibility compliance
the technical standards defining how to make websites accessible to people with disabilities
summary: A set of formal web accessibility recommendations published by the W3C Web Accessibility Initiative.

label: Wearable device
plain_descriptions: electronic gadget worn directly on the human body to monitor activity and health
body-worn tech like smartwatches, fitness rings, and biometric patches
summary: A category of compact electronic devices designed to be comfortably worn on the body or clothing, incorporating sensors, processing, and wireless transceivers for continuous biometric tracking.

label: Web accessibility (a11y)
plain_descriptions: making websites usable for everyone, including people with visual or physical disabilities
building digital products that work seamlessly with assistive tools like screen readers
summary: The inclusive practice of ensuring there are no barriers that prevent interaction with websites by people with physical, sensory, or cognitive disabilities.

label: Web server
plain_descriptions: a computer and software program that delivers web pages to visitors over the internet
the system that listens for web requests and sends back HTML, images, and data
summary: A computer system or software application that processes incoming network requests over HTTP and serves web content to clients.

label: Session
plain_descriptions: the server-side record remembering who you are while you click around a website
the active conversation state linking multiple web page clicks to one logged-in user
summary: A server-side state mechanism that tracks an individual user’s interactions and identity across multiple stateless HTTP requests.

label: Webhook
plain_descriptions: an automatic notification sent between servers as soon as something happens
a reverse phone call where a payment provider rings your app to say money arrived
summary: An automated HTTP POST callback triggered by an origin system to deliver real-time event payloads to external receiver endpoints.

label: WebSocket
plain_descriptions: continuous two-way connection allowing real-time communication between browser and server
persistent bidirectional network socket initiated via an HTTP handshake
summary: A computer communications protocol providing full-duplex, bidirectional communication channels over a single persistent TCP connection initiated via an HTTP upgrade handshake.

label: Wi-Fi
plain_descriptions: ubiquitous wireless radio technology that connects computers, phones, and IoT devices to the internet
high-speed wireless local area network standard operating over 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz bands
summary: A family of wireless network protocols based on the IEEE 802.11 standards used for local area networking of devices and high-speed internet access across licensed-exempt radio bands.

label: Workflow automation
plain_descriptions: setting up if-this-then-that rules that run recurring office chores automatically
connecting software tools so data flows between them without human intervention
summary: The design and execution of automated sequences that pass data and trigger tasks across multiple business tools based on defined logical rules.

label: Working capital
plain_descriptions: cash and short-term assets left over after setting aside money for near-term bills
cushion of operating funds needed to keep daily corporate activities humming
summary: The operational capital buffer calculated as total current assets minus total current liabilities.

label: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
plain_descriptions: a vulnerability where attackers inject malicious javascript into a website to hijack visitor browsers
sneaking rogue code into public comment sections so readers' login cookies get stolen
summary: A web application flaw permitting attackers to embed rogue executable scripts into viewed pages, running unauthorized actions inside visitor browsers.

label: Z-Wave
plain_descriptions: sub-gigahertz wireless mesh protocol for smart homes that avoids crowded Wi-Fi channels
reliable home automation radio standard operating on dedicated sub-1GHz frequencies
summary: A wireless communications protocol operating in the sub-gigahertz frequency spectrum designed specifically for reliable, interference-free mesh networking in residential home automation.

label: Zero-day vulnerability
plain_descriptions: a newly discovered software bug that has no official fix or patch yet
an undisclosed security flaw that attackers exploit before developers know it exists
summary: A previously undisclosed software vulnerability that is actively exploitable or known to attackers before the vendor has developed and released a security patch.

label: Zero trust
plain_descriptions: a security model that never assumes any user or device is safe, even inside the office network
the principle of verifying identity and device health for every single digital request
summary: A cybersecurity framework requiring continuous verification of every user, device, and network transaction, operating under the assumption that breaches are already present.

label: Zigbee
plain_descriptions: low power wireless mesh networking standard commonly used in home automation systems
radio protocol that routes sensor messages across interconnected household devices
summary: A low-power, wireless mesh networking standard built upon IEEE 802.15.4, designed for multi-device home automation and smart energy management.
